messages.content: What's the lowest score in the Flappy Bird game?

function.name: game_tracker_high_score
function.description: Retrieves the highest score recorded in the specified game. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

game_name.description: The name of the game to get the high score for.

username.description: The username of the player. (optional) Default: 'john'

platform.description: The platform where the game was played, i.e PC, Xbox, Playstation, Mobile.

message.content:
In *Flappy Bird*, the very first thing that happens when you play is that you’re given a single “bird” to control. As soon as that bird collides with anything—whether it’s a pipe, the ground, or even the invisible walls at the top—the round ends and your score drops back down to **0**.  

So the absolute lowest score you can ever see in the game is **zero points**, which occurs whenever you fail to pass through even a single pair of pipes.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What's the lowest score in the Flappy Bird game?" They want presumably the minimum possible score or maybe they mean what is the lowest score achieved historically? But likely it's asking about the lowest score you can achieve when playing Flappy Bird - which would be zero if you die immediately after starting.

But we have a tool `game_tracker_high_score` but that's only for retrieving the highest score; not relevant here. There's no mention of low scores. So I think answer should explain that the lowest score is zero because you lose instantly on first collision. Or perhaps ask clarifying question?

Given typical knowledge: In Flappy Bird, each time you hit an obstacle your score resets to zero and ends the run. If you start with one bird and it dies before passing any pipes, your score will be zero. So the lowest score is zero.

Thus respond accordingly. No need to call function.
